span.p:
LAYER-SKIPPING PATH - the one endpoint pair
that bypasses AudioService and calls the repo
and S3 itself. Two consequences: no
@PreAuthorize (SecurityConfig URL rules only,
/api/guest/** permitAll and /api/**
authenticated) and no audit row at all.
The guest route looks up RemovedAtIsNull; the
admin route uses findByAudioCode and so can
serve trashed rows. isPublic is never a gate -
it only picks Cache-Control, public max-age
300 versus no-store.
206 with a Range header, else 200; a missing
S3 object maps to 404, any other S3 fault 500.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
LAYER 2 - business logic. @Transactional on
the class; readOnly=true on getAll, search,
getByAudioCode and getTrash.
SIGNATURES ELIDED - every public method here
and on AudioAPI really ends with two more
params, (Authentication, HttpServletRequest),
threaded down only so the audit row can name
the actor. Dropped from the boxes for width.
getAll and getTrash page in memory via
PaginationSupport.sliceList over a full list;
Pageable never reaches SQL.
requireAdminRole, despite its name and its
message, re-checks the same audio:delete
authority @PreAuthorize already demanded, so
over HTTP it is redundant. It only bites when
restore, purge or getTrash are called from
non-HTTP code.
purge is the only enforced ordering rule: it
rejects a record whose removedAt is still null
with AudioValidationException - trash first.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
LAYER 3a - CACHE READ AND EVICT.
ACTIVE_CACHE is the literal audios:all.
getAllActive is @Cacheable(ACTIVE_CACHE) and
@Transactional(readOnly).
evictAll is @Caching over ACTIVE_CACHE plus
TagSuggestService.CACHE and
KeywordSuggestService.CACHE, because audio
rows carry the tags and keywords feeding the
cross-entity autocompletes.
AudioService calls evictAll after all seven
mutations - create, createAll, update,
setVisibility, delete, restore, purge.
ObjectProvider is lazy on purpose: it breaks
the AudioService to AudioReadCache to
AudioService bean cycle.
CacheConfig side (Caffeine, not Redis):
audios:all is built with maximumSize 1 and
expireAfterWrite 10 minutes - one entry holds
the whole active list, so size eviction never
fires and the TTL is only a backstop behind
evictAll. A new @Cacheable name must be added
to that List or the lookup fails at runtime.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
LAYER 3b - Spring Data JPA.
The trash model lives in the finder
names: RemovedAtIsNull is active,
RemovedAtIsNotNull is trashed.
The @Modifying bulk updates are the
Project cascade path; each bumps
version so a concurrent edit fails
with a stale-version error.
searchByText is a native two-phase
pg_trgm query - but it is NOT what
/api/audio/search runs. AudioService
builds its own SQL through
MediaSearchSqlBuilder and executes
it on EntityManager. searchByText is
the guest path (GuestSearchService).

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
LAYER 4 - S3. Shared by every media
service, not audio-only.
On this path AudioService calls
upload on create, and on update when
a replacement file is sent;
deleteStoredFile guards with
isOurS3Url before deleteFile - on
replace and on purge only.
Soft delete never touches S3, which
is what makes restore work.
getObjectSize and openStreamRange
are reached only from AudioStreamAPI.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
LAYER 5 - AUDIT ROW WRITTEN HERE.
record runs @Transactional(REQUIRES_NEW) so
the log row survives a rollback of its caller.
One audio_audit_logs row per service call:
actor, authorities, permissions, session,
device, IP, request method and path, plus a
denormalized project, person and category.
Read paths log too (READ, LIST, SEARCH), and
purge writes PURGE before the row is deleted
so the record is still readable.
Soft delete writes DELETE - the REMOVE
constant is declared but never used.
